title: Multiomics Study of Corylin in Modulating Longevity and Healthspan_Lysine acetylome
projectDescription: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying Corylin-mediated delay of aging, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach—comprising proteome, phosphoproteome, and lysine acetylome analyses—using tissue samples from quadriceps, kidney, and liver collected from both male and female C57BL/6J mice. Comparative profiling across three groups—young, aged, and aged mice treated with Corylin—enabled a systematic characterization of Corylin-induced molecular alterations associated with aging.
sampleProcessingProtocol: To achieve comprehensive profiling of the proteome, phosphoproteome, and lysine acetylome, we adopted a Tandem Mass Tag (TMT) 10-plex labeling strategy. Each batch included nine experimental tissue samples and one shared reference standard, composed of pooled tumor tissue lysates, to enable accurate relative quantification across samples. Tissue proteins were extracted, trypsin digested, and labeled with TMT reagents and mixed equally. Five percent of the pooled sample was used for global proteome profiling, while the remaining 95% was subjected to sequential enrichment workflows. First, acetylated peptides were enriched using Acetyl-Lysine Motif immunoaffinity beads. The flow-through from this step was subsequently used for phosphopeptide enrichment using TiO₂ beads.  The peptide mixtures were separated and analyzed by online 2D LC-MS/MS using a Dionex UltiMate 3000 nano LC system coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS and MS/MS data were searched against the Swiss-Prot mouse database using Mascot through Proteome Discoverer (version 2.2)
